A minor release that closes three reported issues, finishes the remaining half of two more the
tracker closed alongside 2.0.1, and moves the slice boundary from the shape of a path to the
contents of the filesystem. One new message id is on by default and several existing checks reach
shapes they did not before, so unlike 2.0.1 this can raise your report count as well as lower it.
No option was renamed, no default was flipped for an existing check, and the one new option only
turns a new check off.

## New checks

### `export ... from` is a dependency (#27)

`layers-slices` visited import declarations only, so a re-export bypassed the layer and slice
checks that the equivalent import went through. Re-exports are now visited, judged as the import
of the same path would be and reported where that import would be. In a file under
`src/entities/user`, `export { loginUser } from 'src/features/auth'` now reports:

> You cannot import layer "features" into "entities" (shared -> entities -> features -> widgets -> pages -> processes -> app)

A re-export between two slices of one layer is reported the same way, and so is `export * from`.
Type-only re-exports are exempt under `allowTypeImports`, on by default, in all three spellings:
`export type { X } from`, `export type * from`, and the inline `export { type X } from`.

The report sits where the equivalent import has always put it: on the source string, or on each
offending value specifier when the declaration mixes value and inline type specifiers, so
`export { a, b } from '...'` gives one report and `export { a, type A, b } from '...'` gives two.
On the eight projects measured this added one report, on a statement that already had a
`public-api` report there on 2.0.1.

### The pass-through re-export (`pass-through-reexport`)

Once re-exports are dependencies, a second shape becomes visible: a file that re-exports a
**lower** layer forwards it through its own layer to whoever imports it. Importing downward is
legal, so this is no layer violation, but the higher layer becomes a proxy for the lower one and
the real dependency is hidden. Its message id is `pass-through-reexport`, on by default. In
`src/widgets/nav/index.ts`, `export { createUser } from 'src/entities/user'` reports:

> Re-export from layer "entities" forwards it through "widgets", import it directly instead

The fix is for the consumer to import `src/entities/user` directly. If you use pass-through
barrels deliberately, turn the check off with the new `layersSlices` option
`allowPassThroughReexports: true`, which defaults to `false` and silences this message id alone.
What stays silent, so you can predict the blast radius:

* a re-export that stays inside one slice, which is what a slice public api is made of;
* a re-export between two files of a layer that has no slices, such as `shared` or `app`;
* a type-only re-export in any of its three spellings;
* a re-export of a layer above this one, reported as `can-not-import` instead.

An `index` file is not special: a plain module that re-exports from a lower layer reports too. The
check did not fire once on the eight projects measured, a fact about their barrels rather than
yours, so look before upgrading a large codebase.

### A default import combined with inline type specifiers (#38)

`import config, { type FooType } from 'src/app/config'` was silent, because the declaration was
treated as type-only when every **named** specifier was a type and the default specifier was
never consulted. The default specifier is a value import, so it is now reported.

Where the declaration also carries a value named specifier, `import config, { type FooType, foo }`
goes from one report to two, the extra one on `config` and ahead of `foo` in source order. It is
the only shape measured in which a report that already existed becomes more than one.

## Changed behaviour

### The slice boundary is read from the filesystem

This is the deepest change in the release, and it has no configuration. A path alone cannot tell
a folder inside a slice from a slice of its own, nor a group folder from either, so the plugin
now asks the disk: between the layer and the first configured segment it walks the folders of the
path and settles on the **deepest** one holding a public api file. That means an `index` file and
nothing else, spelled `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.vue` or
`.svelte`, so a colocated `index.d.ts` or `index.test.ts` does not make its folder a slice. Where
no folder in range holds one, or the path will not resolve against the project root, the old path
heuristic decides as before and both sides of a comparison fall back together. Three consequences:

* A folder inside a slice is no longer a slice. `entities/user/hooks` alongside
  `entities/user/components`, with the `index.ts` on `user`, is one slice, and imports between
  the two stop being cross-slice imports.
* A folder name carrying punctuation no longer hides its slice. With an `index.ts` on
  `entities/(shop)/ShopA`, an import reaching past that public api was silent on 2.0.1 and is
  reported here, provided the importing file lies in a slice the plugin can resolve as well. This
  turns on the spelling and not on grouping.
* A folder whose name merely begins with a built-in segment name is no longer cut short. 2.0.1
  matched by prefix and reported an import of `src/features/probe/ui-kit-button` as a deep import
  naming `src/features/probe-kit-button`, which does not exist. That false positive is silent now,
  rechecked against each of the six built-in segment names.

The answer is memoised per directory for the lifetime of the process, which in an editor or
language server outlives a single run, so an `index.ts` you add or delete goes unnoticed until it
restarts; restart the ESLint server before filing a bug about a report that appeared right after
you created or removed one. The added I/O measured as nothing above run-to-run spread.

### Folders that merge into their slice

Several names the old path heuristic called slices now resolve to one folder. The shape to look
for is a folder with an `index.ts` whose sub-folders have none, with something importing across
those sub-folders; an `@x` folder holding no `index` file of its own merges the same way. Most
merges cost nothing, since one costs a report only when something imports across two of the merged
names, and a merge can add a report instead: where an import that now stays inside a slice was
written absolutely, `absolute-relative` reports `must-be-relative-path`. The merged groups, and
the folder spellings behind the punctuation case above, are listed in the measurements file below.

### Two more rules read the `segments` setting (#37, #35)

`absolute-relative` and `no-cross-segment-reexport` resolved a path against the built-in segment
list and ignored the configured one. Both now receive it, and a configured segment name is where
the slice ends. That closes #37, where an absolute import staying inside a single slice went
unreported under a custom segment name and the issue's shape now reports from both directions,
and the other half of #35, whose own example is not a new report: with `segments: ['services']`,
`entities/cart/services/index.ts` re-exporting `../model` reported at the same position and with
the same message on 2.0.1 too.

On folders whose names are not built-in segment names, three movements follow at default options
from the filesystem resolution rather than from the `segments` list. A re-export between two such
siblings holding no `index` file of their own was silent on 2.0.1 and reports here. Where only the
re-exporting folder holds one it is a slice, the re-export crosses nothing, and what reported on
2.0.1 is silent. Where both hold one they are two slices, so `layers-slices` reports
`can-not-import` instead and the rule id on that line changes.

### The layer list and the layer-level `index` check (#34)

The check that flags an `index` file sitting directly on a layer looked only for built-in layer
names and did not fire under a dotted directory. Both are fixed: an `index.ts` on a custom layer
such as `domain` is reported, and a checkout under `.cache/` or `.worktrees/` is checked like any
other. The layer list itself is now normalized where it is read, so a hand written
`settings['@conarti/feature-sliced'].layers` of plain names, or of objects missing `hasSlices`,
answers as the same layers answer through the factory, and an entry that is not an object no
longer throws a `TypeError` out of the rule. `featureSliced()` remains the documented way to
configure the plugin, and still refuses a malformed list. One consequence can silence a report:
`layers: []` is honoured as a project with no layers, so `layers-public-api-not-allowed` stops
firing under it.

## Measured effect

Eight open source FSD projects holding 4071 linted files were linted twice from the same
checkouts at default options, once with 2.0.1 and once with this release. Thirteen reports
appeared and sixteen disappeared, 6600 before against 6597 after, and nothing crashed on either
version. The per project and per rule breakdown is in
[`2.1.0-measurements.md`](https://github.com/conarti/eslint-plugin-feature-sliced/blob/v2.1.0/.github/releases/2.1.0-measurements.md).

## Known limitations

**A relative specifier that climbs above the ESLint working directory.** Point ESLint at a
directory below your project root, typically the FSD root such as `src`, and a relative import
leaving that directory lies under no root the plugin can anchor on, so it is searched as written.
Only when the checkout also sits under a directory carrying a configured layer name does that
search find the layer above and report a violation that is not there. `absolute-relative` reports
it as `must-be-absolute-path` and `layers-slices` now does too; point ESLint's working directory
at the project root to avoid it entirely.

**A dot in the slice folder's own name.** With an `index.ts` on `entities/user.x` and no
`entities/user` beside it, an import that reaches past that public api is silent on 2.0.1 and
reported here, and the report is correct, because the import really is a deep import, but the
path it suggests is cut at the dot to `@/entities/user`, which names no folder; only a dot in
the slice folder itself does this, so a dotted group folder above a slice, such as `shop.group`,
suggests the path it should, and so do `(user)`, `user+x`, `[user]` and `_user` at slice
position.

## Issue status

`#27`, `#37` and `#38` were open against this release and are closed by it.

`#34` and `#35` were already closed on the tracker, in the same batch as 2.0.1. Each of them
had two halves, and 2.0.1 fixed one half of each: the dot-path matching of `ignoreFiles` and
`ignoreImports` for `#34`, and the file name read as a segment for `#35`. The other half of
each is what this release fixes, under the same issue number. Neither has anything outstanding
after this.

`#41` is closed on the tracker too, and this release widens the ground it is closed on. Wherever
the filesystem can resolve the slice, the ambiguity the issue described is gone. Where no folder
in range holds a public api file, the slice is still derived from the path and that ambiguity
stands.
